from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Average Speed Concept", [
            "Average speed equals total distance divided by time.",
            "Visualize this as a line connecting two points.",
            "The line slope represents the average speed."
        ])
        
        # Define elements
        curve = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.1 * x**2, x_range=[-3, 3], color=WHITE)
        p = Dot(color="#FF0000")
        q = Dot(color="#00FF00")
        p_label = MathTex("P", color="#FF0000").scale(0.8)
        q_label = MathTex("Q", color="#00FF00").scale(0.8)
        
        # Position curve in area
        self.place_at_grid(curve, 'C3')
        self.place_at_grid(p, 'E2')
        self.place_at_grid(p_label, 'F2')
        self.place_at_grid(q, 'B5')
        self.place_at_grid(q_label, 'A5')
        
        # Secant line
        secant = Line(p.get_center(), q.get_center(), color="#FFFF00")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.play(Create(curve), Create(p), Write(p_label), Create(q), Write(q_label))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.play(Create(secant))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        slope_label = MathTex(r"\text{slope} = \frac{\Delta y}{\Delta x}", color="#00FFFF").scale(0.7)
        self.place_at_grid(slope_label, 'D4')
        self.play(Write(slope_label))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Problem of 'Instantaneous' Speed", 
                          ["Can we find speed at one exact moment?", 
                           "A single point makes our formula fail.", 
                           "We must shrink the interval to approach zero."])
        
        # --- Animation Content ---
        # A simple path (a curve representing position)
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 4], y_range=[0, 4], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        path = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.25 * x**2, color=WHITE)
        point_p = Dot(axes.c2p(2, 1), color=BLUE)
        
        self.place_at_grid(axes, 'C3', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(path, 'C3', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(point_p, 'C3', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        # Show the division by zero conceptually
        formula = MathTex(r"\frac{\Delta y}{\Delta x} = \frac{0}{0} = ?", color=RED)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'E3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        # Visualize shrinking interval
        point_q = Dot(axes.c2p(3, 2.25), color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(point_q, 'C3', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(FadeIn(point_q))
        
        # Show path of shrinking
        self.play(point_q.animate.move_to(axes.c2p(2.2, 1.21)), run_time=2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "As time shrinks, the secant line tilts.",
            "It eventually becomes a tangent line.",
            "This tangent slope shows instantaneous speed.",
            "Point Q slides closer to point P.",
            "The limit defines the exact rate change."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Limit Process: Approaching the Tangent", lecture_lines)
        
        # Create curve and points
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[0, 4, 1], axis_config={"include_numbers": False}).scale(0.7)
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.25 * x**2, x_range=[0, 4], color=WHITE)
        
        p_x = 2.0
        q_x = 3.5
        
        p = Dot(axes.c2p(p_x, 0.25 * p_x**2), color=BLUE)
        q = Dot(axes.c2p(q_x, 0.25 * q_x**2), color=YELLOW)
        
        label_p = Text("P", font_size=20).next_to(p, DOWN)
        label_q = Text("Q", font_size=20).next_to(q, UP)
        
        secant = Line(p.get_center(), q.get_center(), color=YELLOW)
        
        self.add(axes, curve, p, q, label_p, label_q, secant)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFF00")
        # Animate Q sliding
        def update_secant(mob):
            new_q_pos = axes.c2p(q_tracker.get_value(), 0.25 * q_tracker.get_value()**2)
            q.move_to(new_q_pos)
            label_q.next_to(q, UP)
            mob.put_start_and_end_on(p.get_center(), new_q_pos)
            
        q_tracker = ValueTracker(3.5)
        secant.add_updater(update_secant)
        self.play(q_tracker.animate.set_value(2.2), run_time=3)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")
        tangent = Line(axes.c2p(1, 0.25), axes.c2p(3, 1.25), color=GREEN) # Approximate tangent
        self.play(FadeIn(tangent), FadeOut(secant))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FF00FF")
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Instantaneous Rate of Change and the Derivative

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Average Speed Concept
sections.content: Recall that average speed is total distance divided by total time. Visually, this is the slope of a secant line connecting two distinct points (P and Q) on a position-time graph.
sections.example: A cheetah runs 100 meters in 5 seconds. Average speed = 20 m/s. Visually: A straight line connecting the start and end point on the distance curve.

sections.title: The Problem of 'Instantaneous' Speed
sections.content: What if we want to know the cheetah's speed at exactly 2 seconds? Our standard formula fails because the time interval becomes zero (division by zero). Introduce the idea of shrinking the interval.
sections.example: The cheetah's speedometer shows its exact speed at 2.00s. We move point Q closer and closer to point P on the graph.

sections.title: The Limit Process: Approaching the Tangent
sections.content: Explain that as the time interval Δt approaches zero, the secant line morphs into a tangent line. The slope of this tangent line represents the instantaneous rate of change.
sections.example: Animation: Point Q 'slides' along the curve toward P. The secant line tilts until it matches the curve's slope at exactly point P.

sections.title: Defining the Derivative
sections.content: Formally define the derivative as the limit of the difference quotient: f'(x) = lim(h→0) [f(x+h) - f(x)] / h. This is the mathematical 'tool' to calculate the instantaneous rate of change.
sections.example: Applying the formula to a simple function like f(x) = x² to find the general slope at any point x.

sections.title: Application: Real-world Significance
sections.content: Summarize that the derivative is not just a math symbol; it is the 'local' behavior of a function. Used in physics (velocity), economics (marginal cost), and biology (growth rates).
sections.example: A rocket launch: The derivative tells us the exact vertical velocity at any second t, crucial for ensuring the rocket doesn't break under pressure.
